docs.title: AgentTrace
docs.text:
AgentTrace shows an AI agent's run as a live sequence diagram: one lifeline per participant (the user, the orchestrator, each LLM, tool and sub-agent) and one arrow per event, drawn as it happens. Any past run can be replayed at 0.5×, 1× or 2× speed, or shown at once.

It ships as one Python package, deepagents-trace, imported as agenttrace:

  • a tracking SDK modelled on MLflow's: set_project(), start_run(), log_event(), @agenttrace.trace;
  • a LangChain and deepagents integration: agenttrace.langchain.autolog(), a middleware and two callback handlers;
  • the dashboard: agenttrace ui serves the API, a WebSocket live stream and the web interface, from one Python process (no Node or Bun at runtime).

By default the SDK writes to a SQLite file, ./agenttrace.db, and agenttrace ui reads that same file. Tracing needs no server, no account and no API key.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    agent["Your agent<br/>SDK, autolog, middleware"] -- "writes (default)" --> db[("./agenttrace.db<br/>or PostgreSQL")]
    agent -- "POST /api/events<br/>(http tracking URI)" --> ui["agenttrace ui<br/>API and dashboard"]
    ui --- db
    ui -- "/ws live stream" --> browser["Browser"]

The tracking URI decides where runs go: the default SQLite file, any SQLAlchemy database URL, or a running agenttrace ui over HTTP. The dashboard reads new events from the database, so runs that the SDK writes there directly show up live as well.

docs.title: Pick an integration
docs.text: Your code Use LangChain or deepagents, any setup agenttrace.langchain.autolog(): one line, the agent code doesn't change An agent built for each invocation AgentTraceMiddleware, passed to create_agent or create_deep_agent An async server that reuses a compiled agent, with sub-agents AsyncAgentTraceCallbackHandler, one per request Any other Python code the fluent API Another language POST /api/events

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Installation: the package and its extras.
  • Quickstart: agenttrace ui, then a first trace.
  • Coming from MLflow: the same names, mapped.
  • Event contract: the JSON an agent sends.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: deepagents-trace installs the agenttrace command. agenttrace --version prints the installed version and agenttrace --help lists the commands.

docs.title: agenttrace ui
docs.text:
Serves the API, the /ws live stream and the dashboard.

agenttrace ui [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port 3000] \
              [--database-url URL] [--auth none|password]
Option Default Meaning --host 127.0.0.1 the address to listen on; 0.0.0.0 listens on every interface --port 3000 the port --database-url DATABASE_URL, else sqlite:///./agenttrace.db the SQLAlchemy URL of the database to serve --auth AGENTTRACE_AUTH, else none on a loopback host (127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1) and password on any other the auth mode, see below

It needs the server extra. It first prints a banner: the version, the dashboard URL (localhost when it listens on 0.0.0.0 or ::), the auth mode, the database, with its credentials replaced by *** (user and password together, postgresql://***@db:5432/traces, and any password= query parameter; the absolute path of a relative SQLite file), the AGENTTRACE_TRACKING_URI line for your agents (plus AGENTTRACE_KEY in password mode), and the docs URL. Then the server starts, and creates the tables that don't exist yet. The banner is plain text when the output isn't a terminal or when NO_COLOR is set, which also turns off the colours of the server's log. Stop the server with Ctrl+C.

docs.title: Auth modes
docs.text:
none: no login and no API key. Everything belongs to a single local user, the one the SDK writes as when it writes to the database directly. The server only accepts loopback names in the Host and Origin headers, a guard against DNS rebinding and cross-site requests; AGENTTRACE_ALLOWED_HOSTS=name1,name2 adds names, for example behind a reverse proxy. On a host other than loopback, agenttrace ui warns that anyone who can reach the port can read and write traces, and prints the AGENTTRACE_ALLOWED_HOSTS value to set (with --host 192.168.1.10: AGENTTRACE_ALLOWED_HOSTS=192.168.1.10), or the value already set.

password: accounts (sign up in the browser) and atr_... project keys for sending events; the /ws live stream needs the session cookie. Set AGENTTRACE_SECRET to sign the session cookies: without it, a random secret is used, sign-ins don't survive a restart, and agenttrace ui says so.

docs.title: agenttrace demo
docs.text:
agenttrace demo [--database-url URL]

Loads three demo projects (Customer Support Agent, Research Assistant, Code Review Bot) with their runs, for the local user that --auth none shows. It does nothing if that user already has projects. The database is --database-url, else DATABASE_URL, else ./agenttrace.db. It needs the server extra. In password mode, a signed-in user loads the same projects from Settings → Demo data → Load demo projects.

docs.title: agenttrace db init
docs.text:
agenttrace db init [--database-url URL]

Creates the tables that don't exist yet. There are no migrations: the schema is created as a whole (SQLAlchemy's create_all). agenttrace ui does the same at startup, so db init is for preparing a database ahead of time; it works without the server extra.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Read by Meaning DATABASE_URL ui, demo, db init the database, when --database-url isn't given (default sqlite:///./agenttrace.db) AGENTTRACE_AUTH ui none or password, when --auth isn't given AGENTTRACE_SECRET the server, in password mode the secret that signs session cookies AGENTTRACE_ALLOWED_HOSTS the server comma-separated host names accepted besides loopback: for Host and Origin in --auth none mode, and for the /ws origin check in password mode AGENTTRACE_STATIC_DIR the server serve the dashboard from this directory instead of the bundled one NO_COLOR ui plain-text banner and log AGENTTRACE_TRACKING_URI the SDK where runs go, see tracking URIs AGENTTRACE_PROJECT the SDK the default project (else Default) AGENTTRACE_KEY the SDK the atr_... project key sent to a password-mode server AGENTTRACE_URL the SDK the pre-0.2 ingestion URL (http://host:port/api/events), used when AGENTTRACE_TRACKING_URI is unset

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: agenttrace ui is one Python process: the FastAPI API, the /ws live stream and the dashboard's static files. Deploying it means picking a database, a way to run the process, and what sits in front of it.

docs.title: Docker image
docs.text:
The Dockerfile at the root of the repository builds a single image: a Bun stage builds the dashboard, then a python:3.12-slim stage installs deepagents-trace[server,postgres] and runs agenttrace ui --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3000 as an unprivileged user (uid 10001), in /data. Since it listens on every interface, it runs in password mode.

docker build -t agenttrace .
docker run -p 3000:3000 -e AGENTTRACE_SECRET="$(openssl rand -base64 32)" \
  -v agenttrace-data:/data agenttrace

Without DATABASE_URL, the container uses SQLite at /data/agenttrace.db: keep /data on a volume, as above, or the data goes away with the container. Without AGENTTRACE_SECRET, or with a new value, sign-ins reset at every restart: keep the same secret across runs.

Then sign up in the browser. On the Integration page, Regenerate key creates a project's API key and shows it once, and Settings → Demo data → Load demo projects adds the sample projects. agenttrace demo doesn't help here: it fills the local user of --auth none mode, which password mode doesn't show.

docs.title: Docker Compose, with PostgreSQL
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env
# in .env, set AGENTTRACE_SECRET=<the output of: openssl rand -base64 32>
docker compose up --build

docker-compose.yml runs PostgreSQL 16 (data in the pgdata volume) and the agenttrace service on port 3000, connected through DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://...@db:5432/..., built from POSTGRES_DB, POSTGRES_USER and POSTGRES_PASSWORD (all agenttrace by default). Compose refuses to start until AGENTTRACE_SECRET is set. PostgreSQL isn't published on the host: add a ports: entry to the db service to reach it. docker compose down -v deletes the data.

docs.title: PostgreSQL without Docker
docs.text:
pip install 'deepagents-trace[server,postgres]'
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://agenttrace:secret@db:5432/agenttrace
export AGENTTRACE_SECRET="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
agenttrace db init  # optional: agenttrace ui creates the tables too
agenttrace ui --host 0.0.0.0

There are no migrations: missing tables are created, existing ones are left as they are.

docs.title: Sending runs to a deployment
docs.text:
Point the agents at the server, with a project key:

export AGENTTRACE_TRACKING_URI=https://traces.example.com
export AGENTTRACE_KEY=atr_...

Agents can also write to the database directly (AGENTTRACE_TRACKING_URI=postgresql+psycopg://...), but those runs belong to the local user, which only --auth none shows. With a password-mode server, send them over HTTP.

docs.title: Behind a reverse proxy
docs.text:
Terminate TLS in the proxy and forward everything to the server, including the WebSocket upgrade of /ws (the live diagram needs it), keeping the original Host header. With nginx:

map $http_upgrade $connection_upgrade {
    default upgrade;
    ""      close;
}

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name traces.example.com;
    # ssl_certificate ... ;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection $connection_upgrade;
    }
}
  • Password mode: the /ws origin check compares the browser's Origin with the Host header the server receives. Forward Host, as above, or list the public name in AGENTTRACE_ALLOWED_HOSTS.
  • --auth none: the server only accepts loopback host names, so list the public one: AGENTTRACE_ALLOWED_HOSTS=traces.example.com. Anyone who can reach the proxy can then read and write traces: put authentication in front of it, or use password mode.

docs.title: Live updates
docs.text: The server reads new events from the database every 0.5 seconds, for the runs that someone is watching. That is why runs written straight to the database by the SDK, without going through the server, show up live too.

docs.title: Event contract
docs.text: Agents send runs to agenttrace ui through one endpoint, POST /api/events, from any language. The Python SDK uses it when the tracking URI is http(s)://; when it writes straight to the database (the default), it stores the same runs and events.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Server Request --auth password Authorization: Bearer atr_..., a project key from the Integration page; the run goes to that key's project. No key: 401 {"error": "Missing or invalid API key"}; an unknown key: 401 {"error": "Invalid API key"}. --auth none No Authorization header: the body names the project when it creates a run. A header that is sent anyway is checked as a key. The server only accepts loopback Host and Origin names, plus AGENTTRACE_ALLOWED_HOSTS; others get 403 {"error": "Host not allowed"} or "Origin not allowed".

docs.title: Create a run
docs.text:
{"runId": null, "name": "research run", "project": "support-bot"}

project is only read without a key: that project is created if it doesn't exist yet. name defaults to Untitled run. The answer is 201 {"runId": "<run id>", "event": null}. Without a key and without project: 400 {"error": "project is required when no API key is sent"}.

docs.title: Add an event
docs.text:
{
  "runId": "<run id>",
  "source": "Orchestrator",
  "target": "web_search",
  "type": "tool_call",
  "label": "web_search(rust web frameworks)",
  "payload": {"args": {"query": "rust web frameworks"}},
  "durationMs": 720,
  "status": "ok"
}
Field Required Meaning runId yes the id returned when the run was created source, target yes participant names: the diagram draws one lifeline per name type yes llm_call, tool_call, tool_result, handoff, error or final_answer label no the text on the arrow payload no any JSON, shown in the event's detail panel (default {}) durationMs no an integer status no ok, error or pending (not checked by the server); default error for an error event, else ok

The server numbers the events of a run (seq: 0, 1, 2…) and timestamps them. The answer is 201 {"runId": "<run id>", "event": {...}}, where the event has id, runId, timestamp, seq, source, target, type, label, payload, durationMs and status.

Error Answer source, target or type missing 400 {"error": "source, target, type are required"} unknown type 400 {"error": "type must be one of: error, final_answer, handoff, llm_call, tool_call, tool_result"} unknown run, or a run of another project 404 {"error": "Run not found in this project"} a body that isn't a JSON object 400 {"error": "Invalid JSON body"}

docs.title: End a run
docs.text:
{"runId": "<run id>", "endRun": "completed"}

"failed" ends the run failed; any other value ends it completed. The answer is 200 {"runId": "<run id>", "closed": true, "status": "completed"}. A body with a non-empty endRun only ends the run, whatever else it holds; an empty, false or null endRun is ignored, and the body is read as an event. A run that is never ended stays running.

docs.title: Event types
docs.text: type Usual arrow Payload sent by the SDK llm_call agent → model output_preview, tokens; the middleware and the async handler also send input (system prompt and messages), autolog doesn't tool_call agent → tool args; @agenttrace.trace adds kwargs, and the async handler server (with tool_server=) tool_result tool → agent result (and server); a sub-agent returning, in the async handler: status handoff User → Orchestrator, Orchestrator → sub-agent, or Orchestrator → User the user's message; a hand-off's task; an approval request's actionRequests (status pending) error tool or model → agent error (the exception's class) and message; a run-level failure (on_error()) sends the message alone, as error; a failed sub-agent, status and error final_answer Orchestrator → User answer

docs.title: With curl
docs.text:
Against agenttrace ui on localhost (--auth none):

url=http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/events
post() { curl -s "$url" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$1"; echo; }

run=$(post '{"runId": null, "name": "curl run", "project": "demo"}' \
  | python3 -c 'import json, sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["runId"])')
post '{"runId": "'"$run"'", "source": "Orchestrator", "target": "LLM",
       "type": "llm_call", "label": "plan", "durationMs": 420}'
post '{"runId": "'"$run"'", "endRun": "completed"}'

For a server in password mode, add -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTTRACE_KEY" to post (the key then decides the project).

docs.title: Reading runs back
docs.text: The dashboard reads runs through the same server: GET /api/runs/recent (?limit= up to 50, default 12, and &projectId=) lists the latest runs, and GET /api/runs/<run id> returns one run with its events. In --auth none mode they need nothing else; in password mode they need the session cookie that signing in sets.

docs.title: Live stream: /ws
docs.text:
The browser follows runs over a WebSocket at /ws, with plain JSON messages:

Client sends Server sends {"action": "subscribe", "runId": "..."} {"type": "subscribed", "runId": "..."}, then {"type": "event", "data": {...}} for each new event, and {"type": "run:update", "runId": "...", "patch": {"status": ..., "endedAt": ...}} when the run ends {"action": "unsubscribe", "runId": "..."} {"action": "replay", "runId": "...", "events": [...], "speed": 1} {"type": "replay:event", "data": {...}} for each event, paced by their timestamps divided by speed (all at once for 0), then {"type": "replay:done", "runId": "..."} {"action": "replay:stop", "runId": "..."}

An unknown run, or in password mode another user's run, gets {"type": "error", "runId": "...", "error": "Run not found"}; a connection can follow up to 50 runs. New events are read from the database every 0.5 seconds, so events written by the SDK straight to the database stream too.

In password mode, the connection needs the session cookie, and a browser's Origin must match the host (or be listed in AGENTTRACE_ALLOWED_HOSTS); otherwise it is closed with code 1008. In --auth none mode, the API's Host and Origin check applies.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
AgentTrace is published on PyPI as deepagents-trace. The import, the CLI command and the product are all called agenttrace (that name was already taken on PyPI by an unrelated project). It needs Python 3.10 or later.

pip install 'deepagents-trace[server]'            # the dashboard and the SDK
pip install 'deepagents-trace[langchain,server]'  # plus LangChain, deepagents
pip install deepagents-trace                      # the SDK only

docs.title: Extras
docs.text:
Extra Adds Needed for none sqlalchemy, requests, click the tracking SDK, agenttrace db init server fastapi, uvicorn[standard], bcrypt, itsdangerous, websockets agenttrace ui, agenttrace demo langchain langchain, langchain-core, httpx agenttrace.langchain postgres psycopg[binary] a PostgreSQL database e2e playwright, pytest-playwright the end-to-end tests dev server and langchain, plus pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-mock, httpx working on AgentTrace

Without the server extra, agenttrace ui and agenttrace demo stop with the command that installs it.

docs.title: Check the installation
docs.text:
agenttrace --version
agenttrace demo   # three sample projects, written to ./agenttrace.db
agenttrace ui     # the dashboard, on http://127.0.0.1:3000

docs.title: From a source checkout
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/CouLiBaLy-B/agenttrace && cd agenttrace
pip install -e "./python-server[dev]"
bun install && bun run build:ui  # builds the dashboard

Wheels on PyPI already contain the dashboard. A source install only has it once bun run build:ui has written it to python-server/agenttrace/server/static/; until then, / serves a placeholder page and the API works as usual.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text: One image runs the server and the dashboard, and docker compose adds PostgreSQL. See Deployment.

docs.title: The agenttrace-langchain package
docs.text: agenttrace-langchain is now a deprecated shim over deepagents-trace[langchain]: its imports keep working and emit a DeprecationWarning. New code imports agenttrace.langchain; see Upgrading.

docs.title: Callback handlers
docs.text:
A LangChain callback handler is attached per invocation, through config={"callbacks": [...]}, or for the whole process. Unlike the middleware, it isn't part of the compiled graph, so it also works for an agent that is compiled once and reused. AgentTrace has two handlers:

AgentTraceCallbackHandler AsyncAgentTraceCallbackHandler Attached for the whole process by autolog(), or per invocation per request One run per top-level invocation handler Sends to the tracking URI (./agenttrace.db by default) a running agenttrace ui, over HTTP LLM input (system prompt, messages) not recorded recorded Sub-agents their calls are recorded, on the orchestrator's lifeline each sub-agent has its own lifeline Hand-offs tools whose name contains handoff or delegate the same, plus a tool named exactly task (deepagents) Final answer the last message of the top-level output what the app passes to finish(answer=...) Anonymizer, labels no anonymizer=, phrases=, tool_server=

docs.title: autolog() and AgentTraceCallbackHandler
docs.text:
import agenttrace
import agenttrace.langchain

agenttrace.set_project("support-bot")
agenttrace.langchain.autolog()  # every invocation, from any thread
...
agenttrace.langchain.autolog(disable=True)

autolog() registers one AgentTraceCallbackHandler with LangChain, which adds it to every invocation, including those started on other threads (a FastAPI threadpool, say). Calling it again changes nothing; autolog(disable=True) switches it off.

  • Each top-level invocation becomes one run, named after the top-level runnable (for create_agent, its name), in the current project.
  • Inside agenttrace.start_run(), invocations join that run instead, and the run stays open until the block ends. (The implicit run that log_event() uses outside start_run() is never joined.)
  • Concurrent invocations don't mix: every event goes to the run of its own top-level invocation.
  • It records llm_call (Orchestrator → model: an output preview, the token usage, the duration), tool_call, tool_result and error, a handoff for tools whose name contains handoff or delegate, and a final_answer with the last message of the top-level output. The run then ends failed if an LLM or tool call raised, else completed.
  • Its methods never raise.

You can also pass it explicitly, to trace some invocations only or to give them other options. When autolog is on as well, it leaves those invocations to your handler, so nothing is traced twice:

from agenttrace.langchain import AgentTraceCallbackHandler

handler = AgentTraceCallbackHandler(orchestrator="Planner")
agent.invoke(inputs, config={"callbacks": [handler]})

docs.title: AsyncAgentTraceCallbackHandler: one per request
docs.text:
For an async server that compiles its agent once (cached per user, say), create a handler for each request. One handler traces the main agent and every deepagents sub-agent, because LangGraph passes the callbacks on to nested runs.

from agenttrace.langchain import (
    AsyncAgentTraceCallbackHandler,
    AsyncHttpEventClient,
)

client = AsyncHttpEventClient(url="http://127.0.0.1:3000")  # once, at startup


async def chat(session_id: str, question: str) -> str:
    name = f"chat {session_id}"
    handler = AsyncAgentTraceCallbackHandler(name, client=client)
    handler.on_user_message(question)
    config = {
        "configurable": {"thread_id": session_id},
        "callbacks": [handler],
    }
    answer, status = None, "completed"
    try:
        async for event in agent.astream_events(
            {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": question}]},
            version="v2",
            config=config,
        ):
            ...  # your own streaming to the client
            if event["event"] == "on_chain_end" and not event["parent_ids"]:
                answer = event["data"]["output"]["messages"][-1].content
    except Exception as exc:
        status = "failed"
        handler.on_error(str(exc))
        raise
    finally:
        await handler.finish(status, answer=answer)
        await handler.aclose()  # waits, bounded, until the events are sent
    return answer

Create the handler inside the request: it starts a background task on the running event loop.

docs.title: What it records
docs.text:
Event Arrow Content llm_call agent → model the input (system prompt and messages, or the prompts of a text model), an output preview, the token usage, the duration tool_call, tool_result agent → tool, tool → agent the arguments; the result and the duration handoff Orchestrator → sub-agent for a tool named exactly task, or whose name contains handoff or delegate; the sub-agent is named by the subagent_type, to, name or agent argument tool_result or error sub-agent → Orchestrator when that tool returns, or raises error model or tool → agent an LLM or tool call that raised

"Agent" is Orchestrator or the sub-agent that made the call. deepagents runs a sub-agent behind the task tool, and LangGraph runs the sub-agent's own calls under the task call's namespace: the handler recognises that namespace, on every request of a cached agent. When a sub-agent hands off in turn, the nested sub-agent's calls go to its own lifeline, but its hand-off and return arrows are drawn from and to the Orchestrator. The model's lifeline is named after the model (ls_model_name, else the model id the chat model was built with); a call that names no model reuses the last name seen, so one model doesn't split into two lifelines.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
The handler sees the LLM and tool calls on its own. The app supplies what a callback can't see:

Call Records handler.on_user_message(text) the opening handoff, User → Orchestrator handler.approval_required(info) a human-in-the-loop pause your app detects (from the graph state): a handoff Orchestrator → User, with status pending handler.on_error(message) a run-level failure: an error, Orchestrator → User await handler.finish(status="completed", answer=None) the final_answer (when answer is given), then the end of the run: failed for "failed" or "error", else completed await handler.aclose(timeout=10.0) waits until the queued events are sent (at most timeout seconds), then stops the background task

finish() doesn't wait for the events: a server can send its own response first and call aclose() afterwards, so tracing adds no latency.

docs.title: Where it sends
docs.text:
AsyncHttpEventClient(url=None, api_key=None, timeout=10.0, client=None):

  • url: the server's base URL (http://127.0.0.1:3000) or its full /api/events URL. Default: AGENTTRACE_URL, else http://localhost:3000/api/events.
  • api_key: the atr_... project key; default AGENTTRACE_KEY. Without a key, nothing is sent as Authorization and each run names its project (the current one), which a server running with --auth none accepts. A server that wants a key answers 401, and the run turns off with one warning.
  • client: your own httpx.AsyncClient, to pool connections across requests. Otherwise one is created on first use; AsyncHttpEventClient.aclose() only closes an httpx client it created.

Build one client at startup and share it. Without client=, the handler posts to the tracking URI (set_tracking_uri(), AGENTTRACE_TRACKING_URI), which must then be http:// or https://: anything else raises a ValueError when the handler is created.

docs.title: Anonymizer
docs.text:
anonymizer= takes a function that the handler calls on everything free-form it sends: each event's payload (a JSON-safe dict, in which values that aren't JSON became strings), each label and the run name (strings), and a sub-agent name read from hand-off arguments.

  • Full values first. Values are anonymized whole and truncated afterwards, so a sensitive value cut at a size limit can't slip through as a fragment your patterns no longer match.
  • Fails closed. If the function raises, the field is replaced, never sent unmasked: a payload by {"redacted": "anonymizer failed"}, a label or the run name by [redacted]. A label or run name that comes back as anything but a string is [redacted] too. One warning is logged per run, without the values.
  • Sub-agent names. A name that the anonymizer changes, or fails on, becomes Sub-agent. Names are cut at 60 characters.
  • Participant names (the orchestrator, tools, models, User) are not anonymized.
import re

EMAIL = re.compile(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.]+")


def scrub(value):
    """Mask e-mail addresses in a payload, a label or the run name."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return EMAIL.sub("<email>", value)
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {key: scrub(item) for key, item in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [scrub(item) for item in value]
    return value


handler = AsyncAgentTraceCallbackHandler(
    "chat", client=client, anonymizer=scrub
)

Walk the values rather than running a pattern over json.dumps(...): in JSON text, a newline or an accented letter is an escape sequence, and a pattern that matches across it breaks the JSON.

docs.title: Labels and other options
docs.text:
phrases= overrides the labels below, for example to translate them; {name} and {target} are filled in.

Key Default Label of user_message_fallback user message on_user_message("") tool_result {name} → result a tool result delegate delegate → {target} a hand-off subagent_done {name} → done a sub-agent returning subagent_failed {name} → failed a sub-agent raising approval_required HITL: approval required approval_required() final_answer final answer finish(answer=...) run_failed run failed on_error()

The llm step, llm failed and <tool> failed labels are fixed.

  • tool_server= takes a function of the tool name; its result is added to tool arrows as payload.server, for example the MCP server that ran the tool.
  • orchestrator= renames the main agent's lifeline (default Orchestrator).

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text:
As with the rest of the SDK, tracing never breaks the request: events go to an asyncio.Queue drained by one background task per run, the first failure turns tracing off for that run with one warning, and payloads are bounded (output previews at 240 characters, tool results and the final answer at 500, messages at 500 each and the system prompt at 320 in the LLM input).

Runnable notebook

02_async_callback_handler.ipynb runs a cached agent with a sub-agent, the anonymizer and translated labels offline, against an in-process agenttrace ui.

The 0.2.2 import from agenttrace_langchain import AgentTraceCallbackHandler is this class (deprecated).

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text:
AgentTraceMiddleware is an AgentMiddleware for LangChain's create_agent and deepagents' create_deep_agent. Use it when the agent is built for each invocation: one middleware instance is one run. A server that compiles its agent once and reuses it across requests would trace every request into the same run; it needs a callback handler instead.

from agenttrace.langchain import AgentTraceMiddleware
from deepagents import create_deep_agent

agent = create_deep_agent(
    model=model,
    tools=[web_search],
    middleware=[AgentTraceMiddleware(run_name="research run")],
)
question = "What's the state of Rust web frameworks?"
agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": question}]})

await agent.ainvoke(...) works the same way: the middleware implements the async hooks too.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Argument Default Meaning run_name "deepagents run" the run's name orchestrator "Orchestrator" the name of the agent's lifeline project the current project the run's project, when no API key is used url None post to this server instead of the tracking URI: its base URL (https://traces.example.com) or its /api/events URL api_key None the atr_... project key sent to that server timeout 10.0 HTTP timeout, in seconds

Without url and api_key, the middleware writes to the tracking URI, like the rest of the SDK: ./agenttrace.db by default. Given either one, it posts to url (else AGENTTRACE_URL, else http://localhost:3000/api/events) with api_key (else AGENTTRACE_KEY), as before version 0.2. With a key, the key decides the project.

docs.title: What it records
docs.text:
Hook Event Arrow wrap_model_call llm_call: the input (system prompt and messages), an output preview, the token usage and the duration Orchestrator → model wrap_tool_call, before the call tool_call, with the arguments Orchestrator → tool wrap_tool_call, for a tool whose name contains handoff or delegate also a handoff, to the sub-agent named by the subagent_type, to, name or agent argument (else Sub-agent) Orchestrator → sub-agent wrap_tool_call, after the call tool_result, with the result and the duration tool → Orchestrator wrap_tool_call, when the tool raises error; the exception propagates as usual tool → Orchestrator after_agent final_answer, the last message; the run then ends failed if a tool raised, else completed Orchestrator → User

The run itself is created with its first event. The model's lifeline is named after the model (its model or model_name attribute), else LLM.

The middleware sees only the agent it is attached to. A deepagents sub-agent runs as a separate graph behind the task tool: the middleware records the task call and its result as a plain tool call, but not the sub-agent's own LLM and tool calls. AsyncAgentTraceCallbackHandler records those, on the sub-agent's own lifeline.

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text:
The middleware never gets in the agent's way:

  • non-blocking: events go to a queue that a background thread drains, so model and tool calls never wait for a write. At the end of the run, after_agent waits at most 10 seconds for the queue to drain;
  • never fatal: the first storage or HTTP error turns tracing off for the run, with one warning through logging, and the agent carries on;
  • bounded: tool arguments are cut at 80 characters in the label and 2,000 in the payload, tool results and the final answer at 500, LLM output previews at 240; in the LLM input, each message is cut at 500 characters and the system prompt at 320.

The pre-0.2 import, from agenttrace_langchain import AgentTraceMiddleware, still works through the deprecated agenttrace-langchain package.

docs.title: Coming from MLflow
docs.text:
The tracking API follows MLflow's, so most names carry over.

MLflow AgentTrace mlflow.set_tracking_uri() / MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI agenttrace.set_tracking_uri() / AGENTTRACE_TRACKING_URI mlflow.get_tracking_uri() agenttrace.get_tracking_uri() mlflow.set_experiment() / MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_NAME agenttrace.set_project() / AGENTTRACE_PROJECT mlflow.start_run() / active_run() / end_run() the same names @mlflow.trace @agenttrace.trace mlflow.langchain.autolog() agenttrace.langchain.autolog() MlflowClient agenttrace.AgentTraceClient mlflow ui agenttrace ui

docs.title: What differs
docs.text:
• A run is an ordered list of events, not params and metrics. Each event is one arrow of the diagram: a source, a target, a type (llm_call, tool_call, tool_result, handoff, error or final_answer), and optionally a label, a JSON payload, a duration and a status. See the event contract.
  • A project plays the experiment's part. Projects are created on first use, by name; without set_project() or AGENTTRACE_PROJECT, runs go to Default.
  • start_run() returns the run, which is a context manager: leaving the block ends it completed, or failed if an exception escaped. end_run(status) ends the current run.
  • log_event() and @agenttrace.trace don't block and don't raise (except a ValueError for an unknown event type): each run writes from its own background thread, and a storage error turns tracing off for that run. Ending a run, with end_run() or by leaving the start_run() block, waits for its writes, at most 10 seconds. An exit hook ends and flushes the runs still open, so short scripts don't lose their last events.

docs.title: Tracking URIs
docs.text:
The tracking URI is the first of:

  1. agenttrace.set_tracking_uri(uri);
  2. AGENTTRACE_TRACKING_URI;
  3. AGENTTRACE_URL, the pre-0.2 variable: a full .../api/events URL, of which the server part is used;
  4. http://localhost:3000, when only AGENTTRACE_KEY is set (the pre-0.2 default server; a warning says so once);
  5. sqlite:///./agenttrace.db.
Tracking URI Runs go to sqlite:///./agenttrace.db (the default) or another SQLite file that file, written directly; agenttrace ui reads it (--database-url for another file) another SQLAlchemy URL, such as postgresql+psycopg://... that database, written directly; the tables are created on the first write http://host:port or https://... a running agenttrace ui, through POST /api/events

Over HTTP, AGENTTRACE_KEY is sent when it is set: the run then goes to that key's project, and set_project() is ignored. Without a key, each run names its project, which only a server running with --auth none accepts.

docs.title: The explicit client
docs.text:
Like MlflowClient, AgentTraceClient is synchronous and raises on any error:

from agenttrace import AgentTraceClient

client = AgentTraceClient()  # or AgentTraceClient("postgresql+psycopg://...")
run_id = client.create_run("nightly eval", project="evals")
client.log_event(run_id, source="Orchestrator", target="LLM", type="llm_call")
client.end_run(run_id, "completed")

docs.title: 1. Start the dashboard
docs.text:
pip install 'deepagents-trace[langchain,server]'
agenttrace demo   # optional: three sample projects with their runs
agenttrace ui

agenttrace ui prints where everything is, then serves the dashboard:

    ___                    __ ______
   /   | ____ ____  ____  / //_  __/________ _________
  / /| |/ __ `/ _ \/ __ \/ __/ / / / ___/ __ `/ ___/ _ \
 / ___ / /_/ /  __/ / / / /_  / / / /  / /_/ / /__/  __/
/_/  |_\__, /\___/_/ /_/\__/ /_/ /_/   \__,_/\___/\___/
      /____/

  AgentTrace 0.2.0
  observability for AI agents

  Dashboard   http://127.0.0.1:3000
  Auth        none (no login, no API key)
  Database    sqlite:///./agenttrace.db  (/home/you/my-agent/agenttrace.db)
  Tracking    AGENTTRACE_TRACKING_URI=http://127.0.0.1:3000
              set it where your agents run to send their traces here
  Docs        https://coulibaly-b.github.io/agenttrace/

Open the dashboard URL. On localhost there is no login: everything belongs to one local user. The Database line shows the file the dashboard reads. The SDK writes to ./agenttrace.db too, relative to the directory your agent runs in: run the agent from the same directory, or send its runs over HTTP (step 4).

docs.title: 2. Trace a LangChain or deepagents agent
docs.text:
import agenttrace
import agenttrace.langchain

agenttrace.set_project("support-bot")  # like mlflow.set_experiment()
agenttrace.langchain.autolog()  # like mlflow.langchain.autolog()

agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Where's my order?"}]})

Each top-level invocation becomes one run of the support-bot project. Open it in the dashboard while the agent runs and watch the arrows arrive. The callback handlers page covers what is recorded, and the middleware is the explicit alternative.

docs.title: 3. Trace anything else
docs.text:
import agenttrace

agenttrace.set_project("support-bot")


@agenttrace.trace  # a tool_call, then its tool_result (or an error)
def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    ...


with agenttrace.start_run("triage"):
    agenttrace.log_event(
        source="User", target="Orchestrator", type="handoff",
        label="Where is my order?",
    )
    agenttrace.log_event(
        source="Orchestrator", target="LLM", type="llm_call", duration_ms=480
    )
    web_search("order 4521")
    agenttrace.log_event(
        source="Orchestrator", target="User", type="final_answer",
        label="It shipped yesterday.",
    )

Outside a start_run() block, log_event() and @agenttrace.trace use one implicit run per process, ended by agenttrace.end_run() or when the process exits. Tracing never raises into your code, except a ValueError for an unknown event type: events are written from a background thread, and a storage error turns tracing off for that run, with one logged warning.

docs.title: 4. Send runs from elsewhere
docs.text:
When the agent runs on another machine, in a container or from another directory, send its runs to the dashboard over HTTP:

# the banner's Tracking line; the key only for a server with --auth password
export AGENTTRACE_TRACKING_URI=http://127.0.0.1:3000
export AGENTTRACE_KEY=atr_...

agenttrace ui uses password mode by default when it listens on an address other than localhost. Sign up in the browser; on the Integration page, Regenerate key creates a project key and shows it once.

docs.title: Notebooks
docs.text: Two notebooks run all of the above offline, with scripted models and a temporary SQLite file: python-server/examples/notebooks/.

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
The dashboard has three themes, each with its own palette, typography and motion.

PhosphoreCyanotypeStudio

Dark, like an oscilloscope: phosphor-green glow, monospaced labels, arrows that draw like a beam.

Dark, like a blueprint: drafting-table blues, technical type, arrows that plot in crisply.

Light and calm: paper surfaces, soft shadows, arrows that settle with a spring.

docs.title: Switching themes
docs.text: Use the Theme swatches at the bottom of the sidebar, or Settings → Theme. Auto, the default, follows the operating system: Cyanotype when it is in dark mode, Studio in light mode. The choice is remembered in the browser.

docs.title: Reduced motion
docs.text: Every animation respects the prefers-reduced-motion setting: animations shrink to a short fade, without movement.

docs.title: From deepagents-trace 0.1
docs.text:
The full list is in the python-server README; in short:

  • The server is now the server extra: pip install 'deepagents-trace[server]'. The package alone only carries the SDK (SQLAlchemy, requests, click).
  • On localhost, agenttrace ui now defaults to --auth none: no login, and everything belongs to a single local user, so the projects of existing accounts don't show. Start it with --auth password to keep using accounts and atr_ keys.
  • When only AGENTTRACE_KEY is set, without AGENTTRACE_TRACKING_URI or AGENTTRACE_URL, traces still go to the pre-0.2 default server, http://localhost:3000, with a warning logged once. Set AGENTTRACE_TRACKING_URI to choose.
  • The Next.js backend (Prisma, NextAuth, Socket.IO) is gone, and data from its database is not migrated: start from a new database.
  • With Docker Compose, one agenttrace service replaces web and socket (run docker compose up --build --remove-orphans), AGENTTRACE_SECRET replaces NEXTAUTH_SECRET and is required, and PostgreSQL is no longer published on the host.
  • AgentTraceRun.emit raises a ValueError for an unknown event type instead of dropping the event.

docs.title: From agenttrace-langchain 0.2.x
docs.text:
agenttrace-langchain 0.3.0 is a deprecated shim: it depends on deepagents-trace[langchain]>=0.2.0 and re-exports the old names, which emit a DeprecationWarning, as do the old submodules (agenttrace_langchain.client, .async_client, .run, .async_run, .middleware, .callback, .projection). Move to the new imports:

agenttrace_langchain New import AgentTraceMiddleware agenttrace.langchain.AgentTraceMiddleware AgentTraceCallbackHandler (0.2.2, async) agenttrace.langchain.AsyncAgentTraceCallbackHandler AgentTraceClient agenttrace.tracking.http.HttpEventClient AgentTraceRun agenttrace.tracking.http.AgentTraceRun AsyncAgentTraceClient agenttrace.tracking.async_http.AsyncHttpEventClient, also agenttrace.langchain.AsyncHttpEventClient AsyncAgentTraceRun agenttrace.tracking.async_run.AsyncAgentTraceRun

agenttrace.langchain.AgentTraceCallbackHandler, without Async, is a different class: the sync handler that autolog() installs.

What behaves differently (see the shim README):

  • No API key no longer means no tracing. An async client without a key (api_key=None and no AGENTTRACE_KEY) now posts without an Authorization header, for a local agenttrace ui --auth none; a server that wants a key answers 401 and the run turns off, with one warning. An AgentTraceMiddleware() without url or api_key now writes to the tracking URI: ./agenttrace.db, unless AGENTTRACE_TRACKING_URI, AGENTTRACE_URL or AGENTTRACE_KEY points at a server. If a missing key was your off switch, decide in your app whether to attach tracing.
  • The anonymizer also receives strings. It is called with every payload (a JSON-safe dict), every label (a string) and the run name, and must handle both. If it raises, or returns something other than a string for a label, the field is redacted instead of sent unmasked. See Anonymizer.
  • Stricter hand-offs in the async handler. For AsyncAgentTraceCallbackHandler, only a tool named exactly task, or one whose name contains handoff or delegate, is a hand-off to a sub-agent: create_task, for example, is now a plain tool call. (The middleware never counted task as a hand-off.)
